newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs sold at prices steady to $0.50 per cwt higher early Friday with the market showing signs of starting to recover after its recent slump, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
"We're pretty current, have lighter weights and product is giving a little bit of help," one Illinois dealer said.
There were early trades in Illinois in the country at $56 to $57 and directly to plants at $57.50 per cwt. USDA reported a plant top in Illinois on Thursday of $57.
USDA reported pork cut-out values Thursday were $0.76 to $0.77 per cwt higher.
"We have a balanced market," one Ohio dealer said, noting prices in his areas were around steady.
Dealers noted news that Dakota Pork Industries Inc had closed its facility at Huron, S.D. and sold the plant to John Morrell and Co, a unit of Smithfield Foods Inc.
A spokesman for Smithfield said the company was looking at all its options and in the near term, they would not be killing hogs at the plant.
Dealers said there was some speculation that eventually the move could lead to the resumption of a second shift at Morrell's Sioux City, Iowa plant.
The second shift was cut indefinitely in early February.
